steps.title: The season recital
steps.body:
Twelve weeks end here. They covered dotted rhythms, sections, articulation, honest tempo, composing, strangers, retrieval, a steady left hand, and a portfolio of takes. Two pieces for the family, and one thing you teach.

1. Say the names, play both pieces, hold the last note of each, and bow.
2. Teach someone younger a short tune. Show it slowly, let them try, fix one thing, let them try again.
3. The family asks one question. Answer it.

Then write the long version of the Practice log. Say which trick from this season helped the most, and which piece you would still want to play in a year.

A season built on sections, honesty about tempo, and other people's ears ends the same way every season does. It ends by handing something to someone smaller than you.

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record the recital in one take: both pieces, names said, hands in the frame. If the lesson went well, add a second clip of the tune being taught.
